summary: Provides managerial posture view, KPI strip semantics, and panel-level interpretation guidance.
coverage: How managers should interpret trend changes

warning.title: IMPORTANT
paragraphs: Dashboard conclusions are only as reliable as underlying record and pentest updates. Missing assignment, stale status, or delayed remediation flags will distort KPI interpretation.

sections.title: Dashboard role
paragraphs: The Security Operations Dashboard is the manager-focused analytical surface in RAPTOR. It aggregates inventory and pentest execution data into KPI cards, trend charts, workload views, and recent activity signals.
Use this page for coordination, prioritization, and governance review. It is not a replacement for detailed record editing or pentest authoring.

sections.title: Data and refresh contract
paragraphs: Dashboard data is fetched from `GET /dashboard/data` under `view_dashboard` permission. The response includes records, pentest records, and IP source groups in one request to avoid cross-tab permission dependencies.
Frontend refresh behavior is both automatic and manual. Data refresh runs every 60 seconds and can also be triggered with the explicit refresh action in the header.

sections.title: KPI strip overview
paragraphs: The dashboard top row contains eight KPI cards. Together they provide a compact posture summary for volume, coverage, risk, velocity, and remediation.
Cards should be interpreted as a system. Single-card movement without context can lead to incorrect prioritization.

rows: Current inventory size and source-group breadth.
How much inventory has entered test lifecycle.
Recent closure velocity and fix-rate companion signal.
Incoming finding volume over recent window.
Assets marked remediated in current dataset.

sections.title: Visual panels and intent
paragraphs: Trend charts and supporting cards are arranged to move from broad posture to actionable ownership context. Throughput and vulnerability trends are followed by recent changes, top-risk assets, tester workload, and execution health.
This layout allows managers to identify whether a movement is volume-related, risk-related, or assignment-related before drilling into Security or Records tabs.

rows: Are started and completed tests moving in a balanced direction?
Is finding discovery outpacing resolution or stabilizing?
What meaningful events occurred in the last 30 days?
Which assets currently require fastest attention?
Where is active and open-risk load concentrated by assignee?
How are coverage, fix rate, and in-progress ratio trending together?

sections.title: Manager usage pattern
paragraphs: A practical use pattern is to review coverage and open risk first, then validate whether throughput and workload patterns support current remediation goals.
When anomalies appear, use deep links and filtered security views to confirm whether the issue is assignment bottleneck, data quality gap, or genuine risk increase.
